Install without the internet

Source: vignettes/articles/offline-install.Rmd
offline-install.Rmd

On a laptop, dragonfarm builds its own Python environment the first time it runs. A server behind a firewall can’t, and a team often wants every machine to be exactly the same. For both, dragonfarm ships a lock: every Python package it needs, pinned to one version, with hashes, for Windows, macOS and Linux. This page is for the person who sets machines up.

You need uv and Python 3.12 or later on each machine. The lock comes with the package:

system.file("python", "requirements.lock", package = "dragonfarm")

Same packages everywhere

On a machine with the internet, build the environment from the lock:

uv venv /opt/dragonfarm-py --python 3.12
uv pip sync requirements.lock --python /opt/dragonfarm-py --require-hashes

Then tell dragonfarm to use it, for example in the server’s .Renviron:

DRAGONFARM_PYTHON=/opt/dragonfarm-py/bin/python

(On Windows the interpreter is Scripts\python.exe inside the folder.)

No internet at all

On a machine that has the internet and the same operating system as the target, download the packages into a folder:

uv venv dl --python 3.12 --seed
dl/bin/python -m pip download -r requirements.lock --require-hashes --only-binary=:all: -d wheels

Copy wheels and requirements.lock across, then build with no index:

uv venv /opt/dragonfarm-py --python 3.12
uv pip sync requirements.lock --python /opt/dragonfarm-py --require-hashes --offline --no-index --find-links wheels

On Windows this was about 210 MB of packages. Built this way with an empty cache and no network, the environment came out identical to one built online.

Models come from Hugging Face. Download them on a connected machine, copy the Hugging Face cache folder across, and set HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1. Presets are pinned to exact model versions, so every machine loads the same weights.

Check a machine 

dragon_check()

When DRAGONFARM_PYTHON is set, the check compares the environment with the lock and names any package that differs.

GPUs

The lock is resolved from PyPI. On Windows that gives the CPU build of torch; on Linux, PyPI’s torch already includes CUDA. For a Windows server with an NVIDIA card, add the CUDA build from the PyTorch package index when you download.

One catalogue for the team

Each runs folder keeps a small record of what happened: answers and where they came from, approvals, policies, model versions and who signed them off. On a laptop that is a file in the folder. For a team, point everyone at one Postgres database instead, for example in the server’s .Renviron:

DRAGONFARM_CATALOG=postgresql://dragonfarm:PASSWORD@db.example.com:5432/dragonfarm

The tables are created on first use, and the record stays append-only: the database itself refuses to change or delete past entries. You need the RPostgres package installed.
